entries.content_osis: <div eID="gen32574" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen32575" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen32576" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen32576" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen32575" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen32577" type="x-p"/> The several portions of land appointed for the sanctuary, <reference osisRef="Eze.45.1-Eze.45.5">Eze 45:1-5</reference>, the city, 6, and the prince, <reference osisRef="Eze.45.7">Eze 45:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="Eze.45.8">Eze 45:8</reference>. Regulations concerning the weights and measures, <reference osisRef="Eze.45.9-Eze.45.12">Eze 45:9-12</reference>; with ordinances respecting the provisions for the ordinary and extraordinary sacrifices, <reference osisRef="Eze.45.13-Eze.45.25">Eze 45:13-25</reference>. <div eID="gen32577" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32578" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen32578" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32579" type="x-p"/> When ye shall divide by lot - That is, when on your repossessing your land, every family settles according to the allotment which they formerly had; for it is certain that the land was not divided afresh by lot after the Babylonish captivity. The allotment mentioned and described here was merely for the service of the temple, the use of the priests, and the prince or governor of the people. A division of the whole land is not intended.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 8</hi> <div eID="gen32585" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32586" type="x-p"/> My princes shall no more oppress my people - By exorbitant taxes to maintain profligate courts, or subsidize other powers to help to keep up a system of tyranny in the earth. The former princes even robbed the temple of God to give subsidies to other states.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 10</hi> <div eID="gen32588" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32589" type="x-p"/> Ye shall have just balances - This appreciation of weights, measures, and money was intended to show them that they must not introduce those to which they had been accustomed in the captivity, but those which God had prescribed to their forefathers. See the notes on the parallel places.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 25</hi> <div eID="gen32592" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32593" type="x-p"/> In the seventh month - He shall do at the feast of tabernacles the same things that he was desired to do on the passover. The prince should offer the same number of victims, of the same quality, and with the same ceremonies, as during the above seven days. The offerings were, sin-offerings, burnt-offerings, and peace-offerings.  <chapter eID="Ezek.45"/> <div eID="gen32593" type="x-p"/>
